verdict: Lend selectively to Leh's small owner-run guest houses and restaurants with proven season cash flow and clean title; avoid new large capex and outside-investor-backed projects until local-ownership rules settle.
title: Leh Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Leh hotel or restaurant is a short-season cash machine bolted to a long, cold, closed winter.** Rooms and kitchens earn in the summer trekking and wedding months, then the property sits largely idle; cash must be banked in season to carry fixed costs through winter. **So when a proposal lands, check the season-to-winter cash split first; if the borrower cannot show winter months covered from summer surplus, ask how the gap is funded.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the land and building, not the furniture; cash sits in advance bookings and the season's collections.** Pricing power is real in peak season but thin in shoulder months, and the working-capital cycle is advance-heavy, which is good for us. **Take the booking register and last two seasons' bank statements; if advances are not visible in the account, ask where deposits are held.**

## What has changed now
**Local trade bodies are pushing back on outside investment and on how the official tourism portal was launched [2][3].** That is local news, not a demand signal, and it means ownership and licensing questions around new projects are unsettled. **So for any proposal with an outside investor or a new portal-linked booking arrangement, check the local-ownership position and permits before sanction; if ownership is layered, ask for the full chain.** Peer results are strong but national, not Leh: ITC Hotels Q2 FY27 revenue up 26 percent [4], Ventive Q3 FY26 revenue up 27 percent with 48 percent EBITDA margin [5], Leela Q2 driven by 30 percent RevPAR growth [6]. **Treat these as proof the Indian hotel cycle is healthy, not as Leh numbers; collect Leh occupancy and ARR from customer.**

## Where to grow safely
**Pursue small owner-run guest houses and restaurants with clean title, proven season collections and a local promoter.** Structure as a season-linked working-capital line plus a modest term loan, with covenants on advance-bookings cover and no fresh unapproved capex. **Take the booking register, bank statements and occupancy sheet every month; if advances fall below the agreed cover, ask for the reason and reprice.** Avoid large greenfield capex and outside-investor-backed projects until the local-ownership resolution [3] settles.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch winter cash burn, falling advance bookings and any sign of outside capital entering quietly.** If a borrower starts funding winter from fresh borrowing rather than season surplus, ask for a revised cash plan before renewing. **The data pack gives no Leh score [D], so lean on first principles and these peer results; collect local occupancy, ARR and season length from customer.**
